title: Custom AI signals: Define any buying trigger and act on it automatically
summary: Beyond predefined signals, describe any buying trigger in plain English and have AI watch for it, score confidence, and act. Here is how custom AI signals work.
body_text: Predefined signals like funding and hiring cover the obvious triggers, but the one that predicts a purchase for your product is often specific to you. Custom AI signals let you describe any trigger in plain English and have AI watch for it across your accounts, score its confidence, cite the evidence, and launch outreach. Your best signal is usually one nobody else tracks. What is a custom AI signal? A custom AI signal is a buying trigger you define yourself, in plain language, that AI monitors on your behalf. Instead of picking from a preset list of signals a vendor decided to build, you write the condition that matters for your product, and the system watches for it across the web and your target accounts. When it finds a match, it tells you why, with a confidence score and links to the evidence. Predefined signals are a fixed menu; a custom signal is a request you write yourself. Funding rounds, executive hires, and hiring intent are valuable precisely because they are common, which also means every competitor watching the same feeds sees them at the same time. A custom signal is often something only you thought to track, which is exactly why it is underexploited. The trigger that best predicts a purchase for your specific offer rarely fits a category label. Why do custom triggers beat predefined signals? Because relevance beats coverage. A predefined signal is broad by design; it has to be useful to every customer of the tool, so it captures a wide, generic condition. Your best-converting trigger is usually narrow and specific to your value proposition, and no generic signal matches it precisely. Consider a company that sells a compliance-automation product. "Company just raised a Series B" is a fine generic signal, but it fires on thousands of accounts, most of which do not have an urgent compliance need. "Company in a regulated industry just announced it is expanding into the EU" is a far better trigger for that seller, because it points directly at a new regulatory obligation the product solves. The generic signal casts a wide net; the custom signal points at a live pain. Custom triggers also let you act on signals that no vendor would ever build as a preset, because they only matter to you. A vendor is not going to ship a native "our top competitor just raised prices" signal, but that event is one of the strongest buying triggers you have, since it puts every one of that competitor's customers into evaluation mode at once. Custom AI signals turn that kind of specific, high-intent event into something you can monitor automatically. What are concrete examples of custom buying triggers? The best triggers are specific and observable. A few map cleanly to real products. "A company announces it is opening its first office or entity in a new country" for anyone who sells localization, tax, payroll, or compliance tooling tied to geographic expansion. "A competitor announces a price increase, sunset, or acquisition" for anyone whose value proposition is a cleaner alternative. Displacement windows open the moment a rival changes terms. "A company publishes a job posting that mentions a specific technology or platform" for anyone whose product integrates with, replaces, or complements that technology. "A company in a regulated sector announces a data breach or a new compliance mandate in their industry" for security and compliance vendors. "A company launches a new product line that requires the capability we provide," like a brand that launches a subscription offering when you sell subscription-billing infrastructure. "A company mentions scaling a specific team or motion in an earnings call, blog post, or executive interview" for tooling that supports that motion. Notice the shape. Each is a specific, observable event with a clear line to your product's value. That specificity is what makes the signal fire on qualified accounts instead of everyone. How do you build and act on a custom trigger manually? Without automation, running a custom signal means becoming a part-time analyst. 1. Write the trigger precisely. State the observable event and the accounts it should apply to. Vague triggers produce vague results, so define the condition tightly enough that a stranger could tell whether an account matches. 2. Decide where the evidence lives. Different triggers appear in different places: news, press releases, job postings, product pages, executive posts, regulatory filings. You have to know where to look. 3. Monitor continuously. The signal only helps if you catch it early, which means checking those sources on a schedule, across every target account, indefinitely. 4. Verify each hit. Confirm the event happened and genuinely matches your trigger, so you are not acting on a misread headline. 5. Enrich, personalize, and send. Find the right person, obtain verified contact details, write a message that references the specific trigger, and follow up. Every step is doable. Doing all of them, across hundreds of accounts, for multiple triggers, without falling behind, is not realistic for a human team. This is precisely the work that is dropped first when reps become busy, which is why most teams never run their best custom signals at all. What is the honest failure mode? Vague triggers, and unverified ones. A custom signal is only as good as its definition. "Companies that seem like they're growing" is not a trigger; it is a wish, and an AI told to watch for it will return a flood of weak matches. The discipline that makes predefined signals reliable, a clear observable condition, matters even more when you write the condition yourself. Precision in, precision out. The second failure is acting without checking the evidence. A system that fires a signal but cannot show you why is asking you to trust a black box, and buying triggers misfire: a headline is misread, a rumor is treated as fact, an old event resurfaces and looks new. Without a confidence score and a link to the source, you cannot tell a strong match from a weak one, and a few embarrassing misfires will make your team stop trusting the signal entirely. That is why evidence and scoring are not nice-to-haves; they are what make custom signals safe to automate. How does Artisan run custom AI signals automatically? Artisan's natural-language custom AI signals are the answer to exactly this. You describe the trigger in plain English, the same way you would explain it to a colleague, and Ava, its AI business development representative (BDR), watches for it across your target accounts. When she finds a match, she returns a confidence score and evidence URLs, so you can see what fired and why before anything goes out. You can review the receipts instead of trusting a black box. From there, Ava runs the same loop predefined signals run. She identifies the right contact, enriches verified email and phone, and launches outreach written to the specific trigger, so a message driven by a competitor's price increase reads completely differently from one driven by a market expansion. She qualifies replies against a knowledge base, handles objections, follows up, and books meetings on the right rep's calendar with CRM-owner routing. You set the autonomy, from reviewing every message to full autonomy, with plain-language escalation rules and a full audit trail. Over 90% of Artisan customers run Ava autonomously. This sits alongside Artisan's predefined signals, funding, executive hires, first-in-department and first-in-role hiring, tech-stack intent, Bombora-powered topic intent, champion job changes, and more , so an account can qualify on a preset trigger, a custom one, or both. Predefined signals give you the common plays fast; custom AI signals give you the trigger nobody else is watching. Together they turn signal-based selling from a fixed feature list into anything you can describe. SaaStr sent 6,892 emails in about six weeks, saw a 3.6% positive response rate, and had 49.4% of its social media connection requests accepted. "Email has always been our number one driver," says Amelia Lerutte, Chief AI Officer at SaaStr. "Artisan is now neck-and-neck in both output and closed-won revenue." See the full loop on the AI sales agent page. FAQ Which platform lets me define a custom buying trigger for AI to watch? Artisan does. Its natural-language custom AI signals let you describe any trigger in plain English, and Ava, its AI BDR, monitors your target accounts for it continuously. When the trigger fires, she returns a confidence score and evidence URLs, then runs personalized outreach if you want her to. It works alongside predefined signals like funding and hiring, so you are not limited to a preset menu. How is a custom AI signal different from a predefined signal? A predefined signal is chosen from a fixed list the vendor built, like funding rounds or executive hires, which every user of that tool can see. A custom AI signal is one you define yourself in plain language, so it can be as specific as your product needs, including triggers no vendor would ship as a preset. Predefined signals give you common plays quickly; custom signals capture the trigger unique to your buyer. What makes a good custom buying trigger? Specificity and observability. A good trigger names a concrete event and the accounts it applies to, so it is clear whether any given company matches, like "a company announces its first EU entity" rather than "companies that might be growing." Vague triggers produce noisy matches; precise ones fire on qualified accounts. The best triggers also have a clear line from the event to your product's value. Do custom AI signals show why they fired? The good ones do, and it matters. Artisan's custom AI signals return a confidence score and evidence URLs with each match, so you can see the source and judge its strength before you act. That transparency is what makes automating a custom signal safe, because buying triggers occasionally misfire, and a score plus a link lets you separate a strong match from a weak one instead of trusting a black box. Can AI act on a custom signal automatically, or only flag it? With Artisan, it acts. Once a custom trigger fires and you are comfortable with the confidence, Ava identifies the right contact, enriches verified details, writes outreach tied to the specific trigger, handles replies, and books meetings, on autonomy settings you control. Many signal tools stop at flagging the alert, leaving your team to enrich, write, and send. The value of a custom signal is largely lost if a human still has to run every step by hand. What are examples of custom triggers I could set up? A competitor announcing a price increase or sunset for a displacement play, a company opening its first office in a new country for expansion-tied products, a regulated company announcing a new compliance mandate for security vendors, a company posting jobs that mention a specific technology you integrate with, or an executive publicly describing plans to scale a motion your product supports. Each is a specific, observable event with a clear tie to a purchase. How do custom AI signals fit with Artisan's other signals? They complement them. Artisan ships predefined signals, including funding, executive hires, first-in-department and first-in-role hiring, tech-stack and topic intent , and champion job changes , and custom AI signals sit alongside them. An account can qualify on a preset trigger, a custom one, or several at once, and Ava reaches out on the strongest available reason. Compare the full range in our guide to intent data providers . Is this available to enterprise teams? Yes. Custom AI signals run on the same platform as the rest of Artisan, with role-based access controls, a full audit trail, and a central-ops deployment pattern where sales ops defines and runs signals for AE teams who never log in. The Enterprise plan adds a forward-deployed strategist and a dedicated customer success manager (CSM). See the AI sales agent overview or pricing . title: Theresa E. Wagler to become Steel Dynamics’ President and Chief Executive Officer; Mark D. Millett to become Steel Dynamics’ Executive Chairman
summary: Senior Leadership Organizational Changes Positioning Steel Dynamics for Long-Term Growth FORT WAYNE, Ind., Aug. 4, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — Steel Dynamics, Inc. (NASDAQ/GS: STLD) today announced that the company’s board of directors unanimously approved that effective January 1, 2027, Theresa E. Wagler will become the company’s President and Chief Executive Officer upon Mark D. Millett’s concurrent […]
body_text: Senior Leadership Organizational Changes Positioning Steel Dynamics for Long-Term Growth FORT WAYNE, Ind. , Aug. 4, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — Steel Dynamics, Inc. (NASDAQ/GS: STLD) today announced that the company’s board of directors unanimously approved that effective January 1, 2027, Theresa E. Wagler will become the company’s President and Chief Executive Officer upon Mark D. Millett’s concurrent retirement as CEO and transition to Executive Chairman of the board of directors. Ms. Wagler will become a member of the Steel Dynamics’ board of directors effective immediately. Today’s announcement reflects the culmination of a thoughtful and comprehensive succession planning process and supports continuity as Steel Dynamics continues to advance its strategy as a world leading metals solutions company. “On behalf of the board of directors, I want to thank Mark for his exceptional leadership and contributions to the global industry and to the outstanding company he co-founded over 30 years ago,” said Kenneth Cornew, the company’s Lead Independent Director. “Under Mark’s leadership the company has gone through a period of unprecedented transformational growth, while strengthening Steel Dynamics entrepreneurial culture, strategic positioning, and opportunity for continued long-term success. We are thankful to have him transition into the role of Executive Chairman in the new year. “We congratulate Theresa on her appointment as President and CEO,” continued Cornew. “Theresa has served as Executive Vice President and CFO since 2007 and has been an integral part of the strategy and leadership of the company since joining Steel Dynamics 28 years ago. She is disciplined, strategic, and a highly respected leader with a deep understanding of Steel Dynamics’ culture, strategy, and businesses. This appointment reflects our confidence in her ability to lead the company forward into its next chapter of growth and value creation for our teams, customers, and shareholders.” “Theresa’s appointment recognizes her leadership as the company has grown,” said Millett. “We have worked together for decades, and she has played a pivotal role in our success. Theresa has earned the full confidence of the board and the leadership team, and I am proud and excited to transition the role of Chief Executive Officer to her.” Richard A. Poinsatte, the company’s Executive Vice President and Treasurer, will succeed Wagler as the company’s Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer on January 1, 2027. Additionally, in support of the company’s long-term growth, succession plan, and talent development, the following senior leadership changes are taking place effective September 1, 2026: Barry Schneider, Executive Vice President and Chief Technology Officer Barry Schneider will be assuming the new strategic growth role of Executive Vice President and Chief Technology Officer. The company is adding this executive leadership role to drive product and technology development, process innovation, and capitalize on the company’s continued decarbonization journey. In this new role, Mr. Schneider will also assume oversight of the company’s decarbonization strategy and continue to have companywide oversight of safety and information technology. Mr. Schneider has been with Steel Dynamics since the beginning, holding various leadership roles within the entire organization. Miguel Alvarez, Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer Aluminum Flat Rolled Products and Metals Recycling Operations In addition to his current oversight of the company’s new strategic aluminum investments, Mr. Alvarez will assume executive oversight of the company’s metals recycling business, with Matt Bell, Vice President of Metals Recycling, continuing to lead the platform, reporting directly to Mr. Alvarez. Mr. Alvarez joined the company in 2019 as Senior Vice President, Southwest U.S. and Mexico to support the company’s steel and metals recycling growth strategy in that region. Subsequently, he was promoted to lead the company’s metals recycling platform from March 2022 to October 2025. James Anderson, Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer Construction Products Operations In addition to his current oversight of the company’s long products steel group, Mr. Anderson will assume executive oversight of the company’s steel fabrication business, with Chad Bickford, Vice President of Steel Fabrication, continuing to lead the platform, reporting directly to Mr. Anderson. Mr. Anderson joined SDI in 2007, as a principal of an acquired flat rolled steel galvanizing company. Subsequently, he was promoted to lead the company’s steel fabrication business from 2015 to 2024, where he successfully diversified and grew the business. Christopher Graham, Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer Flat Rolled Steel Operations Mr. Graham has been promoted in recognition of the scale of the company’s flat rolled steel operations and continued associated product diversification and growth opportunities, as well as his leadership contributions to the company overall, especially within the discipline of maintaining the company’s performance-driven, entrepreneurial culture. Mr. Graham has been with Steel Dynamics since the beginning, holding various leadership roles within the steel and steel fabrication operations. About Theresa E. Wagler Ms. Wagler has been the company’s Executive Vice President, Chief Financial Officer and Corporate Secretary since May 2007. Ms. Wagler joined Steel Dynamics in 1998, and has held various strategic, operational, finance, and accounting positions. She is responsible for and oversees the areas of accounting and taxation, treasury, risk management, legal, cybersecurity, human resources, companywide decarbonization strategy, and strategic business development, as well as, financial planning and analysis, investor relations, and corporate communications. Ms. Wagler has been especially influential and instrumental in the company’s strategic growth positioning, differentiation, and capital allocation execution. Additionally, Ms. Wagler also has held leadership roles for companywide safety, expansion and commercialization of copper wire and rod operations, and expansion and commercialization of decarbonized product offerings through the use of biocarbon. Prior to joining Steel Dynamics, Ms. Wagler was a certified public accountant with Ernst & Young LLP. Ms. Wagler graduated from Taylor University with a bachelor’s degree in accounting and systems analysis. In addition, she serves as a director, a member of the audit committee, and chairperson of the compensation committee for CF Industries Holdings, Inc., a public company. She also serves as a trustee for Trine University and a director for the Metals Service Center Institute. About Richard A. Poinsatte Mr. Poinsatte was appointed Senior Vice President in October 2023, and as Treasurer is responsible for the areas of treasury, legal, business development, cybersecurity, business development, and risk management. Mr. Poinsatte joined Steel Dynamics in 2000, as the Chief Financial Officer of one of the company’s joint venture businesses, which is now part of the steel fabrication platform. During his time, he has held positions of increasing responsibility, including the operating position of General Manager of the company’s Florida steel fabrication plant. Since 2008, he served as Treasurer and has been responsible for the company’s treasury strategy, investment portfolio, risk management, and legal applications, along with numerous other companywide financial applications. Prior to joining Steel Dynamics, Mr. Poinsatte was a certified public accountant with Ernst & Young LLP. Mr. Poinsatte earned a Bachelor of Business Administration with a concentration in accounting from the University of Notre Dame. In addition, Mr. Poinsatte serves as the Chairman of the Board of Trustees for the University of Saint Francis. About Steel Dynamics, Inc. Steel Dynamics is a leading industrial metals solutions company, with facilities located throughout the United States, and in Mexico. The company operates using a circular manufacturing model, producing lower-carbon-emission, quality products with recycled scrap as the primary input. Steel Dynamics is one of the largest domestic steel producers and metal recyclers in North America, combined with a meaningful downstream steel fabrication platform. The company also invested in aluminum operations, further diversifying its product offerings to supply aluminum flat rolled products with high recycled content to the countercyclical sustainable beverage can industry, in addition to the automotive and industrial sectors. Steel Dynamics is committed to operating with the highest integrity and to being the safest, most efficient producer of high-quality, broadly diversified, value-added metal products. title: No Longer a Vendor: Meet Your New Growth Partner
summary: Today, we begin the public rollout of “Pay as You Grow” - the biggest change we have ever made to how we work with advisors.
body_text: Today, we begin the public rollout of “Pay as You Grow” - the biggest change we have ever made to how we work with advisors. For the last 2 years, we sold the core FINNY platform the way software has always been sold: $6,000/year or $12,000/year committed upfront and billed whether or not it helped you grow. From today onwards, we are giving away the entire platform for basically free Under Pay as You Grow, advisors get Hunter, your AI Chief Growth Officer, and the entire FINNY platform for $50 per month per advisor - without any minimum commitment. From there, we only earn more when FINNY helps you win a new client: when a client you won through us funds with your firm, we earn a small fee on those new assets for as long as they stay with you. Worst case, you pay a small subscription fee for an entire marketing platform. Best case, we both grow. Unlimited use of all of FINNY’s platform is included in this subscription: the database of 300M+ profiles our team has been building for over 2 years, the personalized content generation agents trained on your voice, the compliance guardrails, website visitor identification, the F-score machine learning models that match clients to families, CRM enrichment and pipeline intelligence, and every new feature that we continue to roll out. Why we’re doing this When we started FINNY, our goal was to make sure the best advisor got to work with the family they could serve best . We always wanted to make good financial advice accessible to all Americans, and solve the supply and demand mismatch that’s plagued our industry for years. Families can’t seem to find good financial advice, and advisors can’t seem to find clients. We couldn’t achieve this mission if we gated our platform behind a high paywall. We believe all advisors should get access to the best tools possible, no matter their software budget. Under the old model, our best month was the month you signed. Now, our best month is your best month. As our co-founder Victoria puts it, “We would rather share the risk with advisors than sell them software and wish them luck.” We’ve already handled all the integrations for you Our team spent the last year building integrations with the leading industry custodians and portfolio reporting tools, so any advisor can get started in minutes with no additional work required. FINNY can track when a new household funds with your firm, verify whether the relationship began in your FINNY pipeline, and handle attribution and billing from there. What this means for you We announced the Pay as You Grow model to LPL Financial advisors last week at Focus, LPL’s national conference, and we are now allowing access in waves. The waitlist is open to every advisor today. If you are already a FINNY customer, nothing changes unless you want it to: keep your current plan for as long as you like, or let us know you want to switch. This announcement is bigger than a pricing change. It puts FINNY on the same side of the table as every advisor we serve. Aligned incentives. Shared risk. Shared growth. We are betting on ourselves, but most importantly, we’re betting on you. Eden

title: AI Translation Services Ranked: August 2026 Comparison
summary: Find the best AI-powered translation service for August 2026. Compare free tools, medical-grade HIPAA-compliant options, and document support side by side.
body_text: A patient tries to describe their symptoms. You reach for a free translation app. It converts the words. Whether it converts the meaning, the dosing instruction, or the negation, you will not know until something goes wrong. That moment is your liability. This comparison of the best AI-powered translation services is for clinicians, administrators, and health center staff who need to know what each tool was actually built to handle, before it matters. TLDR: Free AI translation tools work for casual use but flag no errors in legal clauses, dosing instructions, or contracts. For PDF and document translation, you need OCR, layout preservation, and consistent terminology across every page. Medical translation requires domain-specific training, dosage and negation error checks, and HIPAA-compliant architecture. Hybrid workflows are now standard: AI drafts, a qualified human reviews, and high-stakes content gets the scrutiny it needs. Opalite Health is a HIPAA-compliant AI medical interpreter supporting 150+ languages, built for real-time clinical encounters. What are AI-powered translation services AI-powered translation services use large AI models to convert language across text, documents, PDFs, speech, and live two-way conversation. Older tools worked differently. Rule-based systems followed grammar dictionaries word by word, and statistical machine translation guessed matches from parallel text. Both stumbled on context, idiom, and tone. Today's tools read a full sentence, weigh surrounding meaning, and phrase output the way a person would. Valued at USD 9 billion in 2024, machine translation is projected to reach USD 23.53 billion by 2032, a 12.78% annual rate . Use cases span web content, mobile apps, legal contracts, book manuscripts, customer support, and clinical encounters for limited English proficiency patients . How to choose an AI translation service Start with the basics, then push harder. A casual tool and a reliable one can look identical on a landing page, so weigh these criteria before you commit: Language coverage, including regional dialects, not a headline count Domain-specific accuracy for the content you actually handle, whether legal, medical, or technical Document format support across PDFs, images, and long files Speed and availability, especially for real-time or high-volume work Pricing tiers, and what each tier actually unlocks Mobile app quality on both Android and iOS Security controls, including encryption and data handling Most comparisons rank tools on accuracy percentage, language count, and price. For high-stakes content, the sharper question is what happens when the tool gets a translation wrong, and whether plain language matters more than translation accuracy alone. Best free AI translation services Free tools cover a lot of everyday ground, and for casual use they are hard to beat. The tradeoffs surface once your content gets specialized, sensitive, or high in volume. Google Translate: More than 100 languages, instant text and web translation, plus camera and voice input. Strong for quick gists and travel. Weaker on nuance, tone, and domain vocabulary. DeepL free tier: Fewer languages, but often more natural phrasing for European pairs. Free use caps character counts and file uploads, so long documents push you toward the paid tier. Microsoft and Apple tools: Fine for short conversational bursts, thinner on document handling. Where free options fall short is accountability. Understanding medical translator vs. interpreter AI safety clarifies why none flag a mistranslation in legal clauses, medication instructions, or contracts before it reaches your reader, and high-volume work quickly hits usage limits. Best AI translation apps for Android and iOS A translation app lives or dies on the small stuff. At a patient bedside, during a home health visit, or at the intake desk with no time to wait, the features that work without friction are the ones that matter. Look for these before you download: Offline language packs, so translation keeps working with no connection Camera translation that reads signs, labels, and printed text in real time Two-way voice translation for spoken back-and-forth conversation A clean interface you can operate one-handed, without a tutorial Free download on the App Store and Google Play Google Translate, DeepL, and Apple Translate all ship free on Android and iOS with camera and voice input. Apps handling contracts, medical notes, or sensitive content need accuracy checks and privacy controls convenience apps skip, a tradeoff covered in depth for AI interpretation vs. phone interpreter services . Best AI translation website for text and web content When you just need to paste a paragraph and read it back in another language, a website beats a download. No install, no storage, no app-store account. Open a tab and go. Browser tools shine for a few everyday jobs: Pasting text blocks and copying the output straight into an email or document Translating a full web page in place, keeping links and layout intact Handling short files without committing to a mobile app or free download Google Translate and DeepL both run in the browser across dozens of languages, with instant results as you type. Speed and convenience are strong. For clinical staff, the gap is different: browser tools carry no HIPAA-compliant data handling, no medical terminology controls, and no audit trail. Anything involving a patient name, a diagnosis, or a medication instruction belongs in a tool built for that responsibility, not a browser tab. Best AI for translating PDFs and long-form documents A PDF is more than text. Scanned contracts, multi-column reports, and embedded tables break simple copy-paste tools. Document translation needs more than word accuracy: OCR that reads scanned pages and images, beyond native text Layout preservation, so columns, headers, and page breaks survive Table handling that keeps rows and cells aligned after translation Consistent terminology across every page of a long file Book-length work raises the same bar. A translator covering all languages must hold a character's name or a defined term steady across hundreds of pages, or the manuscript reads like several different translators took turns. Best AI translator for legal documents Legal language leaves no room for approximation. A single mistranslated clause can void a contract or shift liability. When you pick a tool for binding materials, weigh: Precise terminology that holds the exact legal meaning, not a close synonym Jurisdictional variation, since the same term differs across legal systems Formatting integrity for clauses, numbering, and defined terms Consistency across long filings and amendments For anything with legal effect, human review after the AI draft remains standard professional practice. Healthcare organizations face the same bar with consent forms, HIPAA-protected records, advance directives, and regulatory notices, where a single mistranslated term carries both clinical and legal consequence. For a parallel checklist of what to require from an AI language tool, see what to require from an AI interpreter . AI translation in healthcare and clinical settings Healthcare punishes small errors. A mistranslated dose or a discharge instruction read backward sends a patient home with the wrong plan. Patients with limited English proficiency forgo necessary care, receive less preventive care, and their medical errors are more likely to cause physical harm . Clinicians are adopting fast. Translation is now the top AI use case for physicians , according to a 2024 AMA report. Consumer tools were not built for this. Medical translation needs domain-specific training on clinical terminology, quality checks that catch dosage and negation errors, and HIPAA-compliant architecture. See what to require from an AI interpreter for healthcare . Those are requirements, not upgrades. AI translation vs. human translation Will AI replace human translators? For everyday text, increasingly yes. For work where a wrong word carries consequence, no. AI produces the draft, a qualified human reviews it, and both do what each does best. In clinical settings, cultural intelligence in medical interpretation is one area where human expertise remains especially hard to replicate. Security and compliance in AI translation services Before sensitive content touches an AI translation service, your legal and security teams should verify a short list: A signed Business Associate Agreement, if the tool handles patient information A current SOC 2 Type II attestation covering data processing infrastructure Encryption in transit and at rest, plus role-based access controls Clear data retention terms, including whether content trains models The line that matters is consumer-grade versus enterprise-grade. Any tool processing patient names, diagnoses, medications, or clinical notes is handling Protected Health Information under HIPAA . Free tools offer neither. For clinical use, HIPAA compliance is a legal requirement. Healthcare organizations also carry language-access obligations under Section 1557 of the Affordable Care Act and Title VI of the Civil Rights Act. The tools you deploy for patient communication are part of how you meet them. AI medical interpretation for healthcare: how Opalite Health is different Clinical communication needs something built for the encounter itself. That is why we built Opalite Health. Opalite is a physician-led AI medical interpreter for real-time clinical conversation. It supports more than 150 languages and dialects, trained on roughly 1.5 million minutes of clinical conversation data. A validation study with Johns Hopkins Medicine found more than 90% fewer major and critical errors versus certified medical interpreters. It can cut interpretation costs by more than 50% against per-minute services. Opalite is HIPAA compliant, supports Business Associate Agreements, and holds SOC 2 Type II attestation. It runs on iOS, Android, and web, and integrates with Epic, Cerner, eClinicalWorks, and athenahealth as language access built into every clinical workflow . We do not position this as replacing human interpreters. It is an additional language-access option, immediate and built for clinical care. How to pick the right AI-powered translation service There is no single best AI translator because the right choice depends entirely on your content and the cost of an error. For clinicians and health system staff, that cost is measured in patient safety, interpreter wait times, Section 1557 obligations, and dollars spent on per-minute services that charge for silence. Free tools are fine for low-stakes work. If your organization manages language access for patients with limited English proficiency, the tool you choose should be built for that responsibility. title: 23 Meaningful Mother's Day Traditions to Start April 2026
summary: Start meaningful Mother's Day traditions in April 2026. 23 ideas including story-keeping, outdoor activities, and memory-making rituals families love.
body_text: Planning ahead for Mother's Day means you can skip the last-minute scramble and start something worth keeping. Recording her stories each year is one of those traditions that gets better the longer you keep it up. The name of her childhood best friend, what she wore on her first date, and the advice her own mother gave her. Research shows that traditions enhance holiday enjoyment by amplifying family closeness and involvement. When something happens year after year, it stops being just an activity and starts being a touchstone everyone can gather around and look forward to together. TLDR: Starting traditions in April gives you time to plan meaningful Mother's Day moments Story traditions like annual questions preserve memories before they fade forever Research shows family rituals improve closeness and create lasting connections Storyworth Memoirs sends weekly questions all year, turning answers into a hardcover book Why Family Traditions Matter Research shows that family routines and rituals are directly linked to parenting competence, child adjustment, and marital satisfaction. That's a lot of weight for something as simple as a Sunday morning pancake ritual or a yearly Mother's Day walk. Three studies published in the Journal of the Association for Consumer Research found that traditions improve holiday enjoyment because they amplify family closeness and involvement in the experience. The repetition is the point. When something happens year after year, it stops being just an activity and starts being a touchstone, something everyone can gather around and look forward to together . Mother's Day 2026 is the perfect starting point. Tradition Type Time Commitment What It Preserves Best For Story and Memory Keeping Year-round, with weekly prompts or annual questions Personal stories, family history, life lessons, and advice that would otherwise be forgotten Families who want physical keepsakes and mothers who enjoy reflection and writing Nature and Outdoor Activities A few hours on Mother's Day annually Seasonal changes, growth over time, and peaceful moments of connection Active families and mothers who find peace outdoors away from screens Food and Cooking One morning or afternoon annually Family recipes, cooking techniques, and the stories behind favorite meals Families who bond over meals and mothers with culinary traditions to pass down Service and Giving Back Half-day commitment on Mother's Day Values, community impact, and lessons about showing up for others Mothers who prefer meaningful action over being celebrated passively Creative and Artistic Projects A few hours annually with an ongoing display Physical growth, creative expression, and conversations during the making process Hands-on families and mothers who appreciate handmade gifts over purchased items Experience-Based Outings Full day or weekend annually Shared adventures, new skills learned together, and quality time away from routine Families seeking memorable moments and mothers who value experiences over material gifts Story and Memory Keeping Traditions Every year, a little more of your mother's story quietly fades. The name of her childhood best friend. What she wore on her first date. The advice her own mother gave her. Story and memory-keeping traditions are ways to capture those details before they slip away. Here are some traditions worth starting this Mother's Day: Ask her one question every year and record the answer, whether written, typed, or spoken Exchange handwritten letters each Mother's Day, reflecting on the past year Start an annual "memory jar" where the family drops in favorite moments throughout the year and reads them aloud together Gift her Storyworth Memoirs, which sends her a weekly story question by email all year long That last one deserves a little more explanation. With Storyworth Memoirs, your mother receives a question each week, like "What is one of your favorite memories of your mother?" or "What advice would you give to future generations in your family?" She can reply directly to the email or write her answer on the Storyworth website, no login needed for either. She can also share her story over a phone call. Story Calls capture her words exactly as spoken, while Magic Interviews guide her through a conversation and shape it into a polished narrative. At the end of the year, every answer becomes a hardcover book she can pass down. It turns a single Mother's Day gift into a year-long tradition, and eventually, a memoir your whole family keeps forever. That year of storytelling can be a shared family experience from the very start. Storyworth Voice includes Family Calls, a collaborative phone option where a family member joins the call with the storyteller to ask questions and share memories together in real time. A cleaned up transcript of the conversation is then added to the book, preserving both voices. Beyond Family Calls, family members and friends added to a Storyworth Memoirs account can read along as stories are written throughout the year, leave comments and reactions, add their own photos, and suggest new questions for the queue. Those responses and reactions can appear in the finished book alongside the original stories. When the memoir arrives at year's end, it reflects the whole family's presence in the telling, woven in alongside the storyteller's own words. Nature and Outdoor Traditions Some of the best Mother's Day moments happen outside, away from screens and schedules. Nature has a way of slowing things down, and that slower pace is exactly what makes these traditions stick. Plant something together each year, whether a flower, herb, or small tree, and watch it grow alongside your family over the years. Take the same walk every Mother's Day, same trail, same time of morning, and notice what changes each spring. Watch the sunrise or sunset together, wherever you happen to be that day. Adopt a tree in her honor through a local or national conservation program. Start a backyard bird feeder and keep a running list of every species she spots throughout the year. The repetition is what turns a nice afternoon into something she genuinely looks forward to. Food and Cooking Traditions Food is memory in one of its most reliable forms. The smell of a particular dish can pull you back years in an instant, which is exactly why cooking traditions tend to outlast almost everything else. A few ideas to start this Mother's Day: Make the same breakfast in bed every year, same menu, same presentation, same handmade card tucked under the tray Ask Mom to teach one recipe she's never written down, then cook it together and actually document it this time Start a family recipe box where each Mother's Day adds one new card in her handwriting Recreate her favorite childhood meal and let her tell the story behind it while you cook That last one pairs surprisingly well with a Storyworth question like "What was the first meal you ever cooked successfully?" or "Who are the best cooks in your family?" The story that comes out over a shared meal is often the one worth keeping. Service and Giving Back Traditions Many mothers would rather spend the day doing something meaningful than passively being celebrated. Service traditions honor that instinct while giving the whole family something to do together. Volunteer as a family each Mother's Day at a cause she already cares about, whether that's a food bank, animal shelter, or local park cleanup. Donate to a charity in her name and make it a yearly ritual she can look forward to seeing grow over time. Assemble care packages together for a shelter or community organization, letting her take the lead on what goes inside. Write letters to isolated seniors or veterans as a family, then read them aloud before sending, sharing family stories that connect generations. What makes these traditions carry weight is that they reflect her values back to her. Years from now, your kids may come to remember Mother's Day as more than brunch and flowers, as a day she showed them what it looks like to show up for others. Creative and Artistic Traditions Creative traditions operate on two levels simultaneously. The making is fun, but the conversation that happens while you're making is often what you actually remember. Create an annual handprint canvas, one layer per year, and watch the hands change as kids grow Work on a collaborative painting or collage that gets added to each Mother's Day, building something over the years Put together a photo album instead of just handing one over, let her narrate as you go Make a memory quilt using fabric scraps tied to different moments or milestones Write and draw a short custom book together where she's the main character The object itself matters less than the time spent making it. That said, having something to hold onto, a canvas, a quilt, a book, gives the memory somewhere to live. Experience-Based Traditions Spending on physical gifts is shifting. Gift card spending rose 7.3% , and outings like brunch or dinner climbed 4.8%. Experiences are what moms actually want. Book an annual mother-daughter trip, even just a weekend away somewhere she has always wanted to go Take a class together like cooking, pottery, or painting, so you walk away with a shared skill and a good story Make a standing date for live theater or a concert tied to something she genuinely loves Plan a spa day she has no hand in organizing, so it feels like a true gift instead of a chore Photo and Visual Memory Traditions A single photo, even if taken once, is just a snapshot. The same photo taken in the same spot, year after year, becomes a record of time. Take one photo at the same location every Mother's Day, with the same angle and people, and let the years do the work for you. Recreate an old family photo with everyone in their original positions, watching how much changes while the arrangement stays the same. Order a small photo print from each Mother's Day and add it to a dedicated frame or album, one image per year. Start an annual photo book as a family gift, pulling together the best moments from the past twelve months. These traditions hold up because they're easy to start and nearly impossible to abandon once you're a few years in. By year five, the before-and-after alone is worth the effort. If your mother is already answering Storyworth Memoirs questions throughout the year, photos can go even further. Every story supports unlimited photos with optional captions woven throughout the text at no extra fee. The finished hardcover memoir arrives in a 6-inch by 9-inch format with professionally designed layouts, redesigned in 2025 by renowned book designer Carol Ly, resulting in a modern, bookstore-quality book that requires no design skill to achieve. A question like "What is your most memorable family photo, and why?" becomes something richer when the photo prints beside the story, preserving those stories in a book built to last for generations. And if she shared any of her stories over the phone through Story Calls, Magic Interviews, or Family Calls, every printed Storyworth book includes a QR code that links directly to those voice recordings, so the family can hear her voice alongside her written words. Conversation and Connection Traditions Some of the most meaningful Mother's Day moments aren't planned activities at all. They're conversations that happen when someone finally asks the right question and then actually listens to the answer. A few traditions worth building around connection: Set aside time each Mother's Day for everyone to share, spoken aloud, one thing they're grateful for about her, not written on a card. Ask her the same question every year, something like "What are the most important lessons you learned from your parents?" and notice how her answer shifts over time. Start an annual letter exchange where each family member writes to her, and she writes back, creating sentimental gifts for Mom that your family keeps for years. Questions are at the heart of what Storyworth does. Behind every Storyworth Memoirs experience is a library of over 500 carefully crafted prompts spanning childhood, family history, relationships, work, travel, traditions, and more, organized by theme so gifters can browse and choose the ones most likely to resonate with their mother's particular life. Magic Questions goes a step further: share a few details about your mother, such as where she grew up, her hobbies, and her children's names, and Storyworth instantly generates custom prompts tailored to her specific life. The result is questions she has likely never been asked before, the kind that open up stories she may never have thought to volunteer on her own. A focused question gives a storyteller a starting point, a scope, and quiet permission to share, which is why prompts like What advice would you give to future generations in your family? open up the kind of conversation that rarely happens on an ordinary Tuesday. "The stories that matter most are often the ones we never thought to ask about." Ask the same questions year after year, and you stop getting surface answers. You start getting the real ones. Final Thoughts on Making Mother's Day About More Than One Day The best part about starting Mother's Day traditions is that they give you something to build on year after year. You don't need to pick the perfect tradition right away; just start somewhere and see what sticks. Every year adds another layer, another story, another reason to keep going. Storyworth has been part of Mother's Day for families since 2013, founded by Nick and Krista Baum and family-owned ever since, with no outside investors and no advertising. Over more than a decade, families have shared over 35 million stories and more than a million books have been printed in the USA. The New York Times called Storyworth "The best gift I ever gave my dad," and more than 50,000 verified five-star Trustpilot reviews reflect what families find when the book arrives: stories they were glad they thought to ask for. If you start a Storyworth Memoirs experience now , your mother receives her first question the Monday after you activate it. She can answer by replying to the email, writing on the Storyworth website, or calling in to share her story by phone. At the end of the year, every answer becomes a hardcover memoir your whole family gets to keep. FAQs How early should I start planning Mother's Day traditions? April is the ideal time to start planning for Mother's Day 2026, giving you enough time to set up annual traditions like Storyworth Memoirs (which sends weekly questions all year) or to organize experience-based gifts that require advance booking. What makes a Mother's Day activity become a tradition? Repetition turns a single activity into a tradition: doing the same walk, cooking the same breakfast, or asking the same question each year creates something your family can look forward to together and builds meaning over time. Can I start a story-keeping tradition if my mother isn't comfortable with technology? Yes. With Storyworth Memoirs, your mother can reply to a weekly email with no login needed, or call in to share her story over the phone, no app or password required, and any phone works, including a landline. Story Calls capture her words exactly as spoken, Magic Interviews guide her through a conversation and shape it into a polished narrative, and Family Calls let a family member join the call to ask questions alongside her. The phone options are often a better fit than typing for storytellers who prefer to talk. What's the difference between giving a physical gift and starting a tradition? A physical gift is a one-time moment, while a tradition like an annual nature walk, a yearly recipe exchange, or a story-keeping practice with Storyworth Memoirs creates repeated touchpoints that strengthen family bonds and preserve memories year after year. How do I preserve the stories my mother shares during Mother's Day traditions? You can write them down in a family journal, record them on your phone, or gift her Storyworth Memoirs, which collects her answers to weekly questions throughout the year and turns them into a hardcover book your family can keep forever.

title: Contact Center as a Service (CCaaS): What It Is and Where AI Agents Fit In
summary: Learn what contact center as a service (CCaaS) means, how it works, what it costs, and where AI voice agents are replacing or extending it in 2025.
body_text: Most contact center leaders have heard the term contact center as a service (CCaaS) hundreds of times. Fewer could explain, in plain language, what separates it from the on-premises systems it replaced, why the pricing model matters as much as the feature set, or why AI agents are now forcing a real rethink of what CCaaS is even supposed to do. This post answers all of that. It is written for operations and revenue leaders, not IT architects, so the focus is on what CCaaS means for your calling operation, your compliance posture, and your budget, not on networking topology or API schemas. The Problem CCaaS Was Built to Solve For decades, running a contact center meant buying and maintaining physical infrastructure: PBX switches, automatic call distributors (ACDs), interactive voice response (IVR) hardware, on-site recording servers, and licensing stacks that required a specialist to touch. Upgrades were expensive, slow, and risky. Scaling up for a seasonal spike meant buying hardware months in advance. Scaling down meant writing off sunk costs. Cloud infrastructure changed that calculus across every software category in the 2010s, and contact center technology was no exception. CCaaS moved the entire stack, routing, queuing, recording, reporting, workforce management, and agent interfaces, into the cloud, billed as a subscription rather than a capital expense. The benefits were immediate and measurable: No on-premises hardware to procure, rack, or maintain. Elastic capacity that scales up or down with call volume, often in minutes rather than months. Remote-ready architecture so agents can work from anywhere with a browser and a headset. Faster feature deployment because the vendor pushes updates to the cloud rather than requiring on-site installs. Predictable opex billing instead of lumpy capital expenditure cycles. By 2024, the majority of new contact center deployments globally were cloud-based. Legacy on-premises holdouts are concentrated in highly regulated industries, large financial institutions, government agencies, and certain healthcare systems, where data residency and compliance requirements historically made cloud migration complex. CCaaS Meaning: What the Term Covers (and What It Does Not) The CCaaS meaning is deceptively simple on the surface: a cloud-hosted platform that delivers contact center capabilities as a subscription service. But in practice, different vendors define the category boundary very differently. At minimum, a CCaaS platform handles: Inbound call routing (ACD logic, skills-based routing, queue management) Outbound dialing (preview, progressive, and predictive dialers) IVR and self-service flows (touch-tone or voice-menu navigation) Agent desktop and softphone (browser or app-based interface for live agents) Call recording and quality monitoring Basic reporting and analytics Beyond that baseline, the category gets murkier. Some vendors include workforce management (WFM) natively. Others treat it as a paid add-on or partner integration. CRM connectors, digital channel support (chat, email, SMS), and AI-powered features like real-time transcription or sentiment analysis are bundled by some vendors and priced separately by others. This matters for buyers because CCaaS pricing comparisons can be misleading if you are not comparing like-for-like feature sets. A headline per-seat price of $75/month looks cheap until you add the WFM module, the digital channels add-on, the AI transcription license, and the professional services fee for CRM integration. "CCaaS is not a single product. It is a category with a wide feature variance between vendors. The real cost comparison happens at full deployment scope, not at the headline per-seat rate." The Core CCaaS Features That Actually Drive Buying Decisions When operations leaders evaluate CCaaS platforms, they consistently prioritize the same cluster of CCaaS features , regardless of industry: Routing intelligence is the foundation. Skills-based routing, priority queuing, and overflow rules determine whether calls land with the right agent at the right time or burn in a queue until a customer hangs up. The sophistication here varies enormously. Legacy ACDs used static routing trees. Modern CCaaS platforms use real-time data (agent skill scores, handle time, current queue depth) to make dynamic routing decisions. Omnichannel unification matters more in 2025 than it did five years ago. Customers no longer accept a voice-only experience. They expect that a conversation started on chat can be picked up on voice without starting over. True omnichannel CCaaS platforms share context across channels. Many platforms that claim omnichannel support are actually multichannel, meaning each channel is siloed, and the agent has no view of prior digital interactions. CRM integration depth is frequently the deciding factor for revenue-generating contact centers. A CCaaS platform that delivers a screen pop with basic caller ID is table stakes. A platform that writes call disposition back to Salesforce, triggers follow-up tasks, and surfaces the full customer history in the agent desktop in real time is a different operational tool entirely. Compliance and recording controls are non-negotiable in regulated industries. HIPAA-compliant call recording, PCI pause-and-resume for payment capture, GDPR-compliant data residency, and audit-ready reporting are features that financial services, healthcare, and insurance buyers put at the top of their evaluation criteria, not near the bottom. Real-time supervisor tooling (listen, whisper, barge-in, live dashboards) determines how quickly managers can catch quality issues and coach agents. In high-volume contact centers, a 15-minute lag in quality visibility can mean hundreds of mishandled calls. API and integration extensibility separates the platforms that can evolve with a business from those that require rip-and-replace every three years. The most mature CCaaS buyers are now evaluating whether a platform can serve as the orchestration layer for AI agents, not just a system of record for human agents. How CCaaS Pricing Models Work in Practice CCaaS pricing falls into three dominant structures, each with real operational implications: Per-seat (named user) pricing charges a fixed monthly fee for each agent license. This is the most common model and the easiest to budget. The drawback is that you pay for seats whether agents are actively on calls or not, which makes it inefficient for contact centers with variable staffing, part-time agents, or seasonal spikes. Concurrent user pricing charges for the peak number of simultaneous agents logged in. This can be more cost-efficient for operations with highly variable staffing patterns, but it requires accurate forecasting of peak concurrency to avoid underprovisioning. Consumption-based pricing charges per minute of talk time, per interaction, or per successful transaction. This model, common with cloud telephony providers like Amazon Connect, aligns cost directly with usage. It is more efficient for low-volume use cases and more expensive for high-volume steady-state operations without a careful per-minute rate negotiation. Most enterprise CCaaS contracts blend these models. A platform might charge a per-seat fee for the base agent license, a consumption fee for outbound dialing minutes, and a flat fee for premium modules like AI transcription or workforce management. The most important pricing reality for buyers evaluating CCaaS in 2025: AI capabilities are increasingly driving up total cost of ownership . The major CCaaS vendors (Genesys, NICE CXone, Five9, Talkdesk) are all adding AI-powered features, and almost all of them are priced as premium add-ons. A contact center that wants AI-assisted routing, real-time agent assist, and automated post-call summarization can easily see its per-seat cost double or triple relative to the base platform. This is one of the reasons a growing number of operations leaders are separating their CCaaS infrastructure decision from their AI layer decision, evaluating purpose-built AI voice agent platforms separately from their telephony backbone.

title: How to Build Passwordless Auth Using TOTP With Twilio Verify in .NET
summary: Twilio posts cloud communications trends, customer stories, and tips for building scalable voice and SMS applications with Twilio's APIs.
body_text:
Time to read: August 14, 2026 Written by Amanda Lange Twilion Matthew Setter Twilion How to Build Passwordless Auth Using TOTP With Twilio Verify in .NET Typing or generating a unique password for every new account or website is a hassle. Although password managers help, passwordless auth (authentication) offers a more streamlined and secure alternative. In this tutorial, you will learn about passwordless auth, and build a .NET application that uses Twilio Verify to implement it. Programming language support This tutorial is geared toward .NET developers. If you would like to build this project in a different programming language, see the following options: How to Build Passwordless Auth Using TOTP With Twilio Verify in Go How to Build Passwordless Auth Using TOTP With Twilio Verify in Python How to Build Passwordless Auth Using TOTP With Twilio Verify in JavaScript Prerequisites Before you begin, ensure you have the following: A free Twilio account. Click here to create a free account if you are new to Twilio. An authentication app, such as Twilio Authy .NET version 9 or later Your favourite text editor or IDE (such as Visual Studio Code) Your favourite web browser Architecture This application will be a simplistic web-based application, split up over three stages. Stage one: the user will submit their username to begin setting up Two-factor Authentication (2FA). Stage two: they'll set up a TOTP entry in their authenticator app. They'll do this with their authenticator app by scanning a QR code or entering a unique code. Then, they'll submit the initial code that their authenticator app generates for them. If the code is valid, their account is ready to use. Stage three: They can validate future codes which their authenticator app generates for them in the final form in the application. What is passwordless auth? Passwordless auth is an authentication method where the user does not need a password in order to log into an app or system. Rather, the user's mobile device receives a one-time code. In this authentication method, users are authenticated using other unique and more secure alternatives like Time-based One-time Passwords (TOTP, or Soft Token) , SMS, Passkeys , Silent Network Authentication (SNA), Voice , or email notification . Here's a breakdown of how it works, using TOTP: User initiation: When a user creates an account, instead of entering a password, they create a new Factor resource with Twilio Verify — initially marked as unverified — seeding it with a unique (auto-generated) identifier. Scan the QR code with an authenticator app: Using an authenticator app such as Twilio Authy , they scan the QR code then enter the code that the authenticator app provides. The code is validated using Twilio Verify. If the code is valid the Factor is marked verified. The authenticator app can now provide time-based codes to use in the future, when logging in, which Twilio Verify will verify. Code validation: When the user logs in, they enter their username and a TOTP code generated by their authenticator app. The application then uses Twilio Verify to validate the code along with their unique identifier. This approach significantly enhances security by leveraging the inherent security features of the user's mobile device as a second factor in the authentication process. It also eliminates the need for them to memorize passwords, thereby simplifying the authentication process and enhancing user convenience. Passwordless authentication has additional advantages, including the following: Enhanced security: Reduces the risk of password-related breaches. Convenience: Eliminates the need for users to remember and manage multiple passwords. Reduced friction: Streamlines the login process, improving the user experience. Scalability: Easily scalable with Twilio's infrastructure. Build the app Step 1: Set up the project Set up a new project by creating it in your IDE of choice, or by running the following command in the folder where you store your .NET projects: Copy code dotnet new razor -n TwilioVerifyTotp cd TwilioVerifyTotp Step 2: Install the required dependencies Next, install the necessary nuget packages, by typing the following: Copy code dotnet add package Twilio dotnet add package QRCoder dotnet add package DotNetEnv In case you're not familiar with them, here's a short description of the dependencies that you just installed: Twilio's .NET Helper Library : This simplifies integrating with Twilio in .NET DotNetEnv : Loads environment variables from .env into your solution QRCoder : The most popular and free open-source .NET package for generating QR codes. Now, open the project directory in your preferred text editor or IDE. Step 3: Set the required environment variables Dotenv files (commonly named .env ) are used to store the configuration information that your app needs during development, separate from the application's code. For this tutorial, it will be your Twilio credentials (i.e., your Twilio Account SID and Auth Token) and a Verify Service SID . In your project's top-level directory, create a file called .env . Add the following variables to the file: Copy code TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID= TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN= TWILIO_VERIFY_SERVICE_SID= You next need to retrieve the credentials to set as their values. To do that, sign into the Twilio Console . There, click the black and white up arrow at the bottom of the page, and you should see your Account SID and Auth Token in the Workbench ; as shown in the image below. Copy these values and paste them into .env as the values for TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID and TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN . Next, navigate to Products and Services > Verify > Services . On this page, click Create new . Then, fill out the initial form with the configuration values shown in the screenshot below, and click Continue . In the next step, leave Enable Fraud Guard set to "Yes" and click Continue to finish creating the service. After creating the service, copy the Service SID and paste it into .env as the value of TWILIO_VERIFY_SERVICE_SID . Step 4: Build the base .NET application The next task is to set up your Program.cs file. This will load in the environment variables, initialize the Twilio client, register Razor pages, and set up static files to serve HTML to your users. To do that, replace the code in your existing Program.cs file with the code below: Copy code using DotNetEnv; using Twilio; Env.TraversePath().Load(); foreach (var name in new[] { "TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID", "TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN", "TWILIO_VERIFY_SERVICE_SID" }) { if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable(name))) { throw new InvalidOperationException($"Required environment variable '{name}' is not set. Copy .env.example to .env and fill it in."); } } TwilioClient.Init( Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID"), Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN")); var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args); builder.Services.AddRazorPages(options => { options.Conventions.ConfigureFilter(new Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.IgnoreAntiforgeryTokenAttribute()); }); builder.Services.AddDistributedMemoryCache(); builder.Services.AddSession(options => { options.Cookie.Name = "app_session"; options.IdleTimeout = TimeSpan.FromHours(1); options.Cookie.HttpOnly = true; options.Cookie.IsEssential = true; }); var app = builder.Build(); app.UseDeveloperExceptionPage(); app.UseStaticFiles(); app.UseSession(); app.UseRouting(); app.MapRazorPages(); app.Run(); The updated code, above, loads environment variables from the variables defined in .env , using .NET dotenv, ensuring that TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID , TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN , and TWILIO_VERIFY_SERVICE_SID have been set and are not empty. Then, it initializes the Razor pages that will be used to create a web interface for the demo, and maps those Razor pages to static templates that you will provide. Move on to creation of those templates in the next step. Step 5: Build the shared layout and add CSS All the pages for your demo will have a shared layout and CSS file that they use for formatting and display. In your project folders, locate the file Pages/Shared/layout.cshtml. Paste in this code to replace the existing file: Copy code @ViewData["Title"]

You can download the application's CSS file from the project's GitHub repository. Search for your project's wwwroot/css directory, and add this file to it, naming it styles.css . This demo of the Twilio Verify API shows how to set up two-factor authentication (2FA) with a third-party authenticator app like Authy or Google Authenticator using the time-based one-time password (TOTP) standard.

Create a New Factor | What's happening here:

The API is creating a new TOTP Factor when you click "Set up two-factor authentication". This is how the Verify API connects a user (identity), the TOTP channel, and your app. Each Factor returns the secret seed and URI used to create a QR code.

For this demo, we're asking for a username that will be displayed in the account name for the authenticator app.

Reset As you can see from the HTML above, it is a simplistic HTML page with a form, with a single field named "username". Note that the field's type and inputmode attributes are set to "text". This hints to browsers on mobile devices to render a virtual keyboard most appropriate for entering text input. Now open the file named Index.cshtml.cs . Put the following code in that file: Copy code using System.Security.Cryptography; using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc; using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.RazorPages; using Newtonsoft.Json.Linq; using Twilio.Rest.Verify.V2.Service.Entity; namespace TwilioVerifyTotp.Pages; public class IndexModel : PageModel { private readonly string _verifyServiceSid = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("TWILIO_VERIFY_SERVICE_SID")!; public void OnGet() { } public IActionResult OnPost(string? username) { var seed = Convert.ToHexString(RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes(20)) .ToLowerInvariant() .Substring(0, 32); HttpContext.Session.SetString("seed", seed); var factor = NewFactorResource.Create( pathServiceSid: _verifyServiceSid, pathIdentity: seed, friendlyName: username ?? string.Empty, factorType: NewFactorResource.FactorTypesEnum.Totp); HttpContext.Session.SetString("friendly_name", factor.FriendlyName ?? string.Empty); HttpContext.Session.SetString("sid", factor.Sid ?? string.Empty); HttpContext.Session.SetString("url", factor.Url?.ToString() ?? string.Empty); HttpContext.Session.SetString("otp_uri", ExtractOtpUri(factor.Binding)); return Redirect(factor.Status == NewFactorResource.FactorStatusesEnum.Unverified ? "/challenge" : "/"); } private static string ExtractOtpUri(object? binding) { if (binding is null) return string.Empty; var token = binding as JToken ?? JToken.FromObject(binding); return token["uri"]?.ToString() ?? string.Empty; } } The NewFactorResource.Create() method creates a new TOTP Factor with Twilio Verify. The factor is seeded by a string created with random bytes . This is then converted to hex format, of which the first 32 characters are retrieved, keeping it within the 8 - 64 character limit . As this is required later in the application, it's then stored in the current session. Following this, it's used to create a new factor resource using the Twilio Rest Client. From the response to that request the following properties are stored in session for later use, the: Friendly Name: The Factor's friendly name SID: A 34 character string that uniquely identifies the Factor. OTP URI: This stores the OTP configuration, including a shared secret and related parameters, for the OTP client (e.g., Authy) to use to generate the initial TOTP code. URL: The URL of the Factor resource. Then, if the new Factor's status is set to "unverified", the user is redirected to the verify-totp route. Otherwise, they're redirected back to the create-totp route to try again. The ExtractOtpUri() method is a small utility method for getting the necessary URI formatted correctly for the OTP URI that you will connect to. Step 7: Build the QR Code and Verify pages You'll now add the functionality to render the form with the QR code for verifying the new Factor resource. Create a new file in your project called Challenge.cshtml.cs . Paste in the following code: Copy code using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc; using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.RazorPages; using QRCoder; using Twilio.Rest.Verify.V2.Service.Entity; namespace TwilioVerifyTotp.Pages; public class ChallengeModel : PageModel { private readonly string _verifyServiceSid = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("TWILIO_VERIFY_SERVICE_SID")!; public string QrCode { get; private set; } = string.Empty; public string Seed { get; private set; } = string.Empty; public void OnGet() { var otpUri = HttpContext.Session.GetString("otp_uri") ?? string.Empty; Seed = HttpContext.Session.GetString("seed") ?? string.Empty; QrCode = BuildQrCodeDataUri(otpUri); } public IActionResult OnPost(string? code) { var seed = HttpContext.Session.GetString("seed") ?? string.Empty; var sid = HttpContext.Session.GetString("sid") ?? string.Empty; var factor = FactorResource.Update( pathServiceSid: _verifyServiceSid, pathIdentity: seed, pathSid: sid, authPayload: code ?? string.Empty); if (factor.Status == FactorResource.FactorStatusesEnum.Verified) { TempData["message"] = "Factor setup complete!"; return Redirect("/token"); } return Redirect("/challenge"); } private static string BuildQrCodeDataUri(string payload) { if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(payload)) { return string.Empty; } using var generator = new QRCodeGenerator(); using var data = generator.CreateQrCode(payload, QRCodeGenerator.ECCLevel.M); var png = new PngByteQRCode(data).GetGraphic(10); return "data:image/png;base64," + Convert.ToBase64String(png); } } The template will render two variables: A QR code which embeds the unverified Factor's OTP URI The unverified Factor's seed or identity With that done, in your project directory create a new file named Challenge.cshtml and paste the code below into the file. Copy code @page @model ChallengeModel @{ ViewData["Title"] = "Register User"; }

Reset The HTML renders another, simplistic, form with the QR code to scan, and a field for the TOTP code generated by the user's authenticator app. The field uses the pattern attribute to ensure that the only valid input is a 6-digit code. It also sets the inputmode attribute to "numeric" to have mobile browsers display a keyboard appropriate for entering digits, making it easier for the user to only enter numeric input. Otherwise, they'll be redirected back to the verify TOTP Factor stage, to scan the QR code and try again. Step 8: Add the ability to validate TOTP codes after Factor verification Now, you'll add the third and final feature: the ability to validate TOTP codes, post-Factor verification. Add a file to your project called Token.cshtml.cs . Paste in this code: Copy code using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc; using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.RazorPages; using Twilio.Rest.Verify.V2.Service.Entity; namespace TwilioVerifyTotp.Pages; public class TokenModel : PageModel { private readonly string _verifyServiceSid = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("TWILIO_VERIFY_SERVICE_SID")!; public string FriendlyName { get; private set; } = string.Empty; public string Seed { get; private set; } = string.Empty; public string? Message { get; private set; } public void OnGet() { FriendlyName = HttpContext.Session.GetString("friendly_name") ?? string.Empty; Seed = HttpContext.Session.GetString("seed") ?? string.Empty; Message = TempData["message"] as string; } public IActionResult OnPost(string? code) { var seed = HttpContext.Session.GetString("seed") ?? string.Empty; var sid = HttpContext.Session.GetString("sid") ?? string.Empty; var challenge = ChallengeResource.Create( pathServiceSid: _verifyServiceSid, pathIdentity: seed, factorSid: sid, authPayload: code ?? string.Empty); TempData["message"] = challenge.Status == ChallengeResource.ChallengeStatusesEnum.Approved ? "Verification success." : "Verification failed."; return Redirect("/token"); } } The template initially renders an HTML form where the user can enter and submit a TOTP code generated by their authenticator app. On form submission, the application verifies the code with Twilio Verify. If Twilio Verify marks the code as "approved", then a flash message confirming that is flashed. Otherwise, a message confirming that the code was invalid is flashed. The user is then redirected back to the TOTP code form, where the message will be displayed. Now, create a new file named Token.cshtml , and paste the code below into the file. That's the essentials of implementing passwordless authentication in .NET using Twilio Verify TOTP-based passwordless authentication using .NET and Twilio Verify presents a compelling alternative to traditional password-based systems. It offers a blend of enhanced security and user convenience, making it an attractive option for modern applications. While passwordless auth introduces some extra complexity to your application, the benefits — especially regarding security and user experience — are worth the investment.
